thread:
katelyn: Quick follow-up from the RFC meeting. I'm proposing a concrete cutover playbook for moving customers from CP peering -> private endpoint. Main goals: no traffic loss, reversible per-customer, and measurable safety gates. Feedback?

diego: Love the goals. Two operational modes to consider: canary cohort (move 5% of traffic/customers first) vs instant per-tenant switch. Canary gives us app-level signals.

katelyn: Agreed on canary. My rough flow: 1) preflight probes (connectivity + ACL acceptance), 2) enable "canary" private endpoint for tenant, 3) shadow traffic for 15m while primary remains peering, 4) if shadows OK flip primary -> private endpoint; else rollback.

rahul: Shadowing is great but beware of stateful flows. If we shadow only HTTP, TCP sessions won't be validated. We should also run a synthetic TCP/long-lived session probe to detect src-ip or NAT issues.

jen: On src-ip preservation: two supported options - advertise per-tenant egress IP (ENI/EIP) or maintain a consistent NAT pool with sticky mappings per-tenant. ENI gives perfect preservation but doesn't scale for thousands of tenants unless we use shared ENIs + SNAT rules. Sticky NAT is cheaper but requires conntrack-ttl alignment so we don't break sessions during cutover.

diego: Note on conntrack: typical TTLs are 300s. If we change path within that window, connections may still be valid but RPF could fail at customer edge if src-ip differs. So either keep source IP identical or ensure customer firewall tolerates both. We can't rely on customers changing their ACLs.

katelyn: Proposal: default to sticky NAT unless tenant opted into ENI-based preservation. For tenants on BGP we require a manual staged withdraw plan. We'll publish vendor-specific wait windows (e.g., 90s for ProviderX, 4m for ProviderY) and an automated staged-withdraw tool that waits between regions.

rahul: Token & bootstrap handling: during canary we need agents to accept both bootstraps. Suggest issuing a short-lived grace token with TTL = window + 10m and a renewal heartbeat from CP. Also add agent flag accepted_modes=[peering,private] + active_primary. That prevents surprise rotations.

jen: Add agent-side safety: if heartbeat not renewed after TTL, agent should revert to peering-only to avoid stuck dual-mode. Also log state transitions.

katelyn: Observability checklist to gate cutover: shadow_success_rate >= 99.5% over 10m, tcp_probe_success >= 99% over 10m, fallback_rate < 0.5% after flip for 15m, and no increase in 5xx client-facing errors. If any gate fails, auto-rollback.

diego: For rollback we need a clear operator playbook: annotated console button "rollback tenant" that flips primary, revokes new routes, and re-issues tokens. Also run a postmortem checklist capturing probe diffs and NAT churn.

rahul: BGP specifics: do NOT withdraw all CP announcements at once. Use a wave strategy: withdraw in one CP region, wait convergence window, then next region. Provide a table mapping carrier/provider -> conservative wait windows and automated retries.

jen: API shape for SEs: POST /cutovers with body { tenants: [...], strategy: "canary|per-tenant|staged-bgp", canary_percent: 5, window: "2026-05-01T01:00Z/03:00Z", preserve_src: "nat|eni|opt-in" } plus dry-run mode that returns a plan and risk hints.

katelyn: Good. Also add a "shadow-only" dry-run that doesn't flip primary but verifies all probes and NAT behavior for a tenant.

diego: Metrics to add ASAP: per-tenant primary_mode, shadow_success_pct, tcp_probe_latency_p50/p95, nat_mapping_churn, route-withdraw-timestamps, and a synthetic request trace that shows end-to-end latency deltas.

rahul: Security note: secrets for preflight probes should be scoped and rotated after cutover. Don't reuse bootstrap tokens for probes. Use a single-use probe token TTL of 15m.

jen: Ops-bot: can we schedule a dry-run next Tuesday in staging? infra-bot: planned-run scheduled for 2026-04-06T22:00Z - running shadow-only passes for a small test cohort.

katelyn: Thanks. Action items: katelyn -> draft playbook + default gate numbers; diego -> observability panel mock; rahul -> BGP wait-window table + withdraw script; jen -> API + agent heartbeat semantics. I'll post draft RFC in this thread once ready. :rocket:
